qualification: Portable canonical VMM network adapter and host-tested x86 packet path
observations: The production VMM adapter compiles with real SDK headers on aarch64 and x86_64, using an explicit MMIO base, IRQ and mapped queue region. The ARM wrapper retains its prior defaults.

ASan/UBSan host test verified exact packet bytes and used-ring lengths through the real libvmm net backend, GPA translator, canonical loopback pump and x86 IOAPIC. Both TX and RX asserted GSI 18 and acknowledgment lowered it.
Invalid initial placement performs no attachment. Failed attachment registers no guest device. Rebinding preserves a queued packet and does not attach again.
The full Spark gate retained the existing ARM guest network, block and console proofs.
limitations: The x86 packet test mocks kernel IPC and uses the canonical loopback pump. It does not prove an Intel host NIC or Linux x86 networking.
Root network grants, persistent wakeups and host NIC integration remain outstanding for the Intel board.
Canonical integration, pinned Debian acceptance, GUI qualification and v0.4 release remain incomplete.
